kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea YELLOW/ADVISORY - The Halema'uma'u eruption of Kīlauea is paused following episode 57 fountaining on the morning of November 23. Summit inflation has restarted indicating that another episode is likely in the coming weeks.
kilauea_notices.detail: Overview: A VAN/VONA lowering the alert level from ORANGE/WATCH to YELLOW/ADVISORY was issued in response to the end of episode 57: https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-HVO-2026-11-23T12:00:58+00:00 Details and a chronology of episode 57 are included in a status report are presented here: https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-HVO-2026-11-23T17:33:15+00:00 Episode 57 lava fountaining occurred from the north vent from 12:15 a.m. to 6:00 a.m. HST on November 23, 2026, following approximately 23 hours of precursory overflows from both the north and southwest vents. The lava fountain reached around 650 feet (200 meters) above the vent before gradually declining in height and ending abruptly at 6:00 a.m. HST. The lava flows from this eruption covered up to 50% of the crater floor that may continue to creep forward over the next several days. The lava fountain generated a plume that reached up to 20,000 feet above sea level (6,000 meters) that was dispersed to the south and southwest by light trade winds. Summit tilt at UWD deflated by 18 microradians during episode 57. Upon the end of episode 57 lava fountaining, summit tiltmeters changed from deflation to inflation, indicating that another episode is likely in the coming weeks. Summit Observations: Currently, the summit vents are emitting plumes of volcanic gas and remained incandescent around dawn just after the end of episode 57 fountaining. Since the end of episode 57 at 6:00 a.m. HST, tilt at UWD has inflated by 1.3 microradians after losing approximately 18 microradians during episode 57. Other summit tiltmeters also show a change from deflation to inflation following the end of episode 57. Seismicity followed the normal pattern by returning to low-level tremor with bursts every 5-10 minutes following the end of episode 57. Four earthquakes were located within the summit region over the past day. Winds remain out of the north to northeast, blowing the gas plume to the south and southwest. The gas array measured approximately 1200 t/d of SO2 yesterday (November 22, 2026). Rift Zone Observations: Rates of seismicity and ground deformation remain low in the East Rift Zone and Southwest Rift Zone. SO2 emissions from the East Rift Zone remain below the detection limit. Analysis: Following the end of episode 57 on November 23, 2026, summit tiltmeters have recorded a typical post-fountaining recovery, with continuous inflationary tilt at UWD. The abrupt switch from summit deflation to inflation at the end of episode 57, continued glow from the vents, and the resumption of low frequency tremor bursts indicate that another lava fountaining episode is likely in the coming weeks. It is too early to accurately forecast when any future episode might occur. Kīlauea has been erupting episodically since December 23, 2024, from two primary vents (north and south) within Halemaʻumaʻu at the summit. Lava fountaining episodes generally last less than 12 hours and are separated by pauses of two or more weeks. HVO continues to closely monitor Kīlauea and remains in contact with Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park and the Hawaiʻi County Civil Defense Agency regarding eruptive hazards. Summary of episode 57 (Episode 57 Status Report): Lava fountaining occurred between 12:10 p.m. and 6:01 p.m. on November 5, 2026. Maximum fountain heights were about 660 feet (200 meters). Only the north vent produced fountaining. Tephra fallout was primarily towards the southwest, in closed areas of Hawai'i Volcanoes National Park, with trace amounts on Highway 11. The eruptive plume rose as high as 18,000 feet (5,500 meters) above sea level. Tiltmeter data indicate approximately 8 million cubic yards (6 million cubic meters) of lava were erupted, with an average eruption rate of 260 cubic yards (200 cubic meters) per second. mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts were within typical levels in October, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a slight increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 66 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the October reporting period, after 53 in September. These variations are within the typical range for the past two years. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
